subject: APAC region: latency & 5xx spike — cross-region failover initiated
messages:
From: ops@astrahealth.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: ceo@astrahealth.com
Date: Sun, 12 Mar 2028 02:14:00 +0000
Subject: Production 5xx + latency spike in APAC - immediate help needed

Hi Kimberly,

We're seeing a large increase in 5xx responses and median latency in our APAC footprint (ap-northeast-2 / AZ B). Impact started ~01:50Z and has been steady for 18 minutes. Error rate climbed to ~17% and p50 latency is ~1.2s (baseline ~120ms). This is affecting core auth and API endpoints — we have customers reporting failed checkouts.

Attached: astra_5xx_sample.log, request_traces_02-14Z.json.

Immediate ask: can Redwood divert traffic out of the impacted AZ or activate a cross-region fallback? We need anything that will reduce 5xxs and restore latency within the next 30 minutes. Please escalate to SRE/Exec if needed.

Thanks,
Sam Rogers
Ops Lead, AstraHealth
ops@astrahealth.com

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: ops@astrahealth.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 12 Mar 2028 02:19:12 +0000
Subject: Re: Production 5xx + latency spike in APAC - immediate help needed

Sam — thanks for the data, and sorry you're seeing this. We're treating as Sev2->Sev1 risk given error rate and customer impact. Plan below (executing now):

1) Start proactive drain of affected AZ (ap-northeast-2b) and route new sessions to ap-southeast-1 and ap-northeast-1.
2) Spin up pre-warmed capacity in ap-southeast-1 (small burst pool) to absorb traffic.
3) Apply temporary routing override (short TTL) and enable circuit-breaker relax for retries for 5 minutes.
4) Collect and stream additional traces to your team for correlation.

Aditya / Rishi — can you confirm the drain + route override command now? Monica / Grace — looping you for customer comms and exec briefing. I'll update in 10 minutes with metrics.

Attachments: playbook_failover_checklist.pdf

Kimberly Park
Head of SRE - Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 12 Mar 2028 02:22:45 +0000
Subject: Re: Production 5xx + latency spike in APAC - immediate help needed

On Sun, 12 Mar 2028 at 02:19 +0000 kimberly_park@redwood.com wrote:
> Sam — thanks for the data, and sorry you're seeing this. We're treating as Sev2->Sev1 risk given error rate and customer impact. Plan below (executing now):
>
> 1) Start proactive drain of affected AZ (ap-northeast-2b) and route new sessions to ap-southeast-1 and ap-northeast-1.

Confirmed. Quick diagnostics:
- Synthetic probes show a spike in queue depth on inference nodes in ap-northeast-2b starting 01:48Z (avg queue depth x6).
- Autoscaler logs indicate repeated failure to allocate new pods due to transient NVMe mount errors (see snippet).
- KV-cache miss rate increased which magnifies token compute.

Actions executed at 02:21Z:
- Marked ap-northeast-2b state=draining (no new sessions).
- Applied routing override: route policy APAC_PRIMARY -> prefer ap-southeast-1, fallback ap-northeast-1; TTL 60s.
- Provisioned burst capacity (t2-small pool) in ap-southeast-1 and warmed model instances.

I'm monitoring token throughput and 5xx rate; early signal shows 5xx rate falling to ~6% and p50 latency down to 420ms for routed traffic. Will post another update in 5 minutes.

Aditya Rao
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: ops@astrahealth.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: ceo@astrahealth.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 12 Mar 2028 02:28:03 +0000
Subject: Re: Production 5xx + latency spike in APAC - immediate help needed

Sam — Monica from Redwood CS here. We're escalating to execs and your account team. Brief update for your leadership: we've initiated a controlled traffic redirection to nearby regions while SREs remediate the underlying node allocation failure.

We understand the business impact; if this is a P1 for AstraHealth, we'll open a credit review and commit to a prioritized postmortem. Kimberly and Aditya will lead the technical remediation, Grace will coordinate the post-incident timeline and customer comms.

I'll set up a short bridge for a live status update at 03:00Z unless you prefer we keep working async.

Monica Patel
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: ops@astrahealth.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 12 Mar 2028 02:33:58 +0000
Subject: Update: cross-region routing active, monitoring recovery metrics

On Sun, 12 Mar 2028 at 02:22 +0000 aditya_rao@redwood.com wrote:
> Confirmed. Quick diagnostics: ... Actions executed at 02:21Z: Marked ap-northeast-2b state=draining ...

Team — short status:
- Routing override live at 02:21Z. ~85% of new session traffic is now landing in ap-southeast-1 and ap-northeast-1.
- Measured effect: 5xx rate for user-facing endpoints reduced from 17% -> 4.8% across routed traffic; p50 latency for routed traffic ~360ms.
- Underlying NVMe mount failures are still being investigated by infra; Rishi is heading node-level remediation.

Next steps (owner):
- Rishi: continue remediation and determine when ap-northeast-2b can safely accept traffic (ETA 40–90m).
- Aditya: keep scaling warm pools and monitor KV-cache rebuild behavior.
- Monica/Grace: run customer comms; prepare one-page incident summary and credit path.

I'll hold routing override until we have sustained error rate <1% for 10 minutes or explicit sign-off.

Kimberly Park
Head of SRE - Redwood Inference

To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
